questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose University of Sydney and Australia in general because I realised that I may never have the same opportunity to travel so far away for such a long period. It was crucial that it was an English speaking country as well. It can't complain about Australia also has really nice weather and beaches :-)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. We were assigned a supervisor from USYD that we could contact. At times it was difficult to get ahold of her as she had annual leave.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't recall getting any assistance once I arrived in Sydney.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived off campus but in student accommodation (Queen Mary Building). This accommodation was guaranteed if applied through the university. My advice would be to apply for the accommodation through the university and also doing it ASAP when you receive the e-mail about applications being open.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Queen Mary Building is situated just a short walk from campus (5-10 min, 20 min to law school). Groceries are a bit further away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is a bit confusing. You receive an e-mail with a document with a link to a spreadsheet with the courses available to exchange students. When applying for enrolment, you also put your preferences for the courses. At some point the supervisor will let you know which courses has been approved for you, and you then have to apply (as far as I remember) again for the courses. During the first week of the semester, you can drop courses and apply for new ones after having been to class. The supervisor helps with this once they've sent out an e-mail with instructions about it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As previously mentioned, the supervisor is very helpful with course registration. I even know that it is possible to apply for courses that are not usually available for exchange students. I did not do this myself, so I am unsure how successful such an application is.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got approved for all the courses (I applied to 8-10) I applied to but one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When you have the option to apply for 8-10 courses, apply for all of them. This will ensure pre-approval for the course and then you don't have to worry about the classes being full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had tried to apply for the BA courses (they pretty much offer all courses as both BA and MA level). I was assigned only MA courses by the University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is a lot less case based and more lecture based. I only had seminars but it was very rare for anyone to raise their hand. Professors encouraged being active in class but it seemed that no one was interested. Some professors offer powerpoint slides, others don't. One teacher had no slides and spoke for 1 hour constantly without asking any questions for the students to answer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Rule of Law and its Value - MA course 
Criminology - MA course
Federal Constitutional Law - MA course
Media Law: Defamation and Privacy - MA course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I CANNOT recommend Federal Constitutional Law. This class was very difficult to follow as it required a lot of prerequisite knowledge, and the sit-in pen and paper exam was tough. It was interesting, though, to learn about the constitution of Australia. 
Criminology is very international, and so it was easy to follow as an exchange student. 
Media Law is very common law based, so it was interesting to learn about from a Danish perspective. The exam(s) are multiple assignments during the semester (one where you choose the topic yourself), so it is not too difficult to do during the semester.
Rule of Law and Its Value was just ok. The professor is very engaged in the different theories and the exam is just two assignments (one of them with a topic you choose yourself)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a cleaning fee that you have to pay once you move in to the Queen Mary Building of about 126 AUD (as far as I remember). Also there is a fee for paying rent with international bank accounts (I paid an additional 44 AUD each month for this fee).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going to restaurants etc. is usually cheaper than in CPH. Groceries are somewhat cheaper than Denmark (some fresh produce is VERY expensive since it is not native to Australia and must be shipped in). Public transportation is very cheap (especially if you manage to get ahold of a student concession card).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There a multiple clubs (I joined the run club, food adventure society). There are always different events by the clubs and the student union (USU) hosts events every week (usually for free). There are clubs for all ethnicities pretty much and for all kinds of hobbies and interests.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the clubs!! This is a great way of meeting people, getting a free meal etc. and so much fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travelling! It's allowed to drive with a Danish license in New South Wales, Tasmania and Queensland, and it is not very expensive to rent a car. I also loved going to the beach, walk around Sydney or going to national parks (Royal National Park, Blue Mountains etc.) to hike.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Australia is not exactly the same as Denmark, but it is not that different either.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Australian students are not very easy to socialise with. I mostly made friends with other exchange students and a few domestic students living at the Queen Mary Building.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are quite friendly which is nice. There is a normal culture of it being allowed to bring your own drinks to restaurants which is plus!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared that the academic level is confusing. The professors seem to make it very very difficult, but then when you look at the requirements for the class, it does not seem that difficult. I still have not received all my grades, so I am unsure what the expectations are.
Get the student concession Opal card! It makes the public transportation almost free. You apply through the opal card website.
Drop courses that don't feel right within the first weeks of classes!!! You will regret not doing it :,(

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting lots of amazing people, seeing beautiful nature and the personal growth!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It is difficult being away from family, partners, friends etc. and it specially is difficult because of the time zone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
